summary: Iter-8 security hardening tested end-to-end. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter8_security.py covering SEC-001 SSRF (7 blocked variants + legit URL regression), SEC-002 voicemail host allowlist (DB-verified: attacker recording URL results in fallback body, no fetch attempted), SEC-003 CORS wildcard/credentials guard (OPTIONS preflight from attacker origin: ACAC != true), SEC-004 Twilio signature validation (a: fall-open when no auth_token; b: reject when auth_token set & no signature — verified no consent transition recorded; c: valid signature acceptance — FAILS due to real backend proxy-URL bug), plus regression checks (plans, login, scribe templates, sms compliance profile) and frontend smoke on /roi, /app/inbox, /app/team, /app/integrations (0 console errors). 21/22 pytest tests pass. The single failure surfaces a real production bug in signature validation.

critical.issue: SEC-004 signature validation calls RequestValidator.validate(str(request.url), ...). Behind the kubernetes ingress, request.url = 'http://pet-care-helper-1.cluster-2.preview.emergentcf.cloud/...' — different scheme AND host from the public Twilio-facing URL 'https://pet-care-helper-1.preview.emergentagent.com/...'. Result: every legitimate Twilio POST with a valid signature will fail validation and return 'This number is not configured', effectively disabling all inbound Twilio traffic for any clinic that supplies an auth_token. Confirmed via DIAG log: url='http://pet-care-helper-1.cluster-2.preview.emergentcf.cloud/api/twilio/sms/inbound/...' — signature signed against the https public URL is rejected.

action_items: SEC-004 URL reconstruction: in twilio_service._validate_twilio_signature (and/or add a global ProxyHeadersMiddleware), rebuild the URL Twilio would have signed using X-Forwarded-Proto + X-Forwarded-Host (or the Host header) before calling RequestValidator.validate. Suggested minimal patch: fwd_proto = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto') or request.url.scheme; fwd_host = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-host') or request.headers.get('host') or request.url.netloc; signed_url = f"{fwd_proto}://{fwd_host}{request.url.path}" (append '?' + query if present). Alternative: run uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*' so str(request.url) already reflects the public https URL. Retest test_c after the fix.
Once fixed, main agent can also verify signature validation logs (currently there's a helpful 'Rejected inbound webhook — invalid signature' warning — keep it).

rca of the issue: SEC-004c failing signature validation — RCA: FastAPI's request.url reflects the socket-level scheme/host uvicorn is bound to (0.0.0.0:8001 → internal cluster hostname over HTTP). The kubernetes ingress terminates TLS and rewrites Host, so Twilio (or our test) sign the URL 'https://pet-care-helper-1.preview.emergentagent.com/...' while the backend validates against 'http://pet-care-helper-1.cluster-2.preview.emergentcf.cloud/...'. HMAC-SHA1 of two different strings never match. Reproduction: temporarily add `logger.warning(f'url={str(request.url)!r}')` inside _validate_twilio_signature, POST any signed request, and observe the internal URL in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Mitigation options: (1) reconstruct URL from X-Forwarded-Proto + X-Forwarded-Host headers before validating; (2) add starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware or run uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'. Option (1) is safer because it doesn't trust upstream headers globally — validate them only inside the signature check where a mismatch is caller-controlled anyway.
